title: Can Diplomacy Prevent Escalation?
text:
Diplomats often insist that quiet negotiation is more effective than public confrontation, since rivals who are not humiliated in front of their own citizens are more willing to compromise. Back-channel talks allow each party to test proposals without committing to them publicly. Critics, however, argue that secrecy can leave ordinary citizens uninformed about decisions that affect their security.

Yet the value of discretion depends on whether it is accompanied by genuine accountability. Agreements reached privately must eventually be submitted to legislatures and courts, otherwise they risk being dismissed as bargains struck behind closed doors. Thus, the most durable diplomacy combines confidential exploration with transparent ratification.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why are rivals more willing to compromise in quiet negotiations?
options: They are not humiliated in front of their own citizens
They receive financial rewards from third parties
They are forced to comply by international courts
They avoid all media attention permanently

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what must privately reached agreements eventually be submitted to?
What can be inferred about the author's view of secret diplomacy?
options: It is always unacceptable in international relations
It is useful only when it leads to public accountability
It should replace all public debate
It is ineffective under any circumstances

questions.text: Why does the author describe unratified private agreements as 'bargains struck behind closed doors'?
options: Because such deals may be dismissed as illegitimate without public approval
Because such deals always involve physical violence
Because diplomats prefer to keep no records of any agreement
Because courts are unable to examine secret documents

vocabulary.definition: a direct and often hostile meeting or clash between opposing sides
the practice of keeping information hidden from others
careful behaviour that keeps sensitive matters private
formal approval that makes an agreement legally binding

paragraph_translations: Diplomatlar, sessiz müzakerenin kamuoyu önünde yapılan çatışmalardan daha etkili olduğunu sıklıkla savunur; çünkü kendi vatandaşları önünde küçük düşürülmeyen rakipler uzlaşmaya daha istekli olur. Gayriresmî görüşmeler, her tarafın önerileri kamuoyu önünde taahhüt etmeden denemesine olanak tanır. Ancak eleştirmenler, gizliliğin sıradan vatandaşları kendi güvenliklerini etkileyen kararlardan habersiz bırakabileceğini ileri sürer.

Yine de gizliliğin değeri, bunun gerçek bir hesap verebilirlikle birlikte olup olmadığına bağlıdır. Gizlice ulaşılan anlaşmaların sonunda yasama meclislerine ve mahkemelere sunulması gerekir; aksi halde kapalı kapılar ardında yapılan pazarlıklar olarak görülme riski doğar. Bu nedenle en kalıcı diplomasi, gizli ön hazırlığı şeffaf onayla birleştirendir.
